transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that... my sleep has just gotten really, really messed up lately. I mean, it's completely out of whack. I’ll go to bed, and I’ll just end up staying up half the night with my mind just running and running. Like, I do bookkeeping for work, so I'm looking at spreadsheets and numbers all day, and you'd think my brain would be exhausted by the time I get home, but it just won't shut off. I'll be laying there in the dark thinking about invoices, or just completely random stuff from years ago, and I just watch the clock go from midnight to two to three in the morning. 

And then, on the flip side, sometimes I'll actually manage to fall asleep, but then I'll wake up way, way too early. Like, 4 AM, pitch black outside, and I just can't get back to sleep, but I feel awful, like I never even rested at all. My body feels heavy, but my eyes are just wide open. I tried drinking that sleepytime chamomile tea, I tried turning off my screens an hour before bed because I read about the blue light thing, but it doesn't matter. It's just... I'm either staring at the ceiling for hours because my thoughts won't stop, or I'm up before the sun feeling totally drained, and I just don't know how to fix it on my own anymore.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, not just work-related tasks like bookkeeping?

Um... no, not really. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting there fretting about, you know, whether I left the stove on, or if my car is going to break down, or what I'm going to make for dinner on Thursday. My mom is a huge worrier, she worries about literally everything—like if the mailman is ten minutes late she thinks something terrible happened—but I'm really not like that at all. 

It's less about *worrying* and more just... noise? Like, even with the bookkeeping stuff I mentioned, when I'm laying there, it's not that I'm anxious or stressed about the invoices. It's just that I'm *thinking* about them. Like I can literally picture the Excel cells and the formulas in my head. Or, I don't know, I'll think about a movie I watched three weeks ago and try to remember the lead actor's name, and then I'll think about what else that actor was in, and then I'm thinking about the popcorn I ate at the theater, and then I'm wondering how popcorn is actually harvested... it's just this endless chain of completely random stuff. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I'm worrying about everyday things. I mean, I pay my rent, I go to work, I get my groceries, and none of that really stresses me out or makes me bite my nails or anything. My brain is just more like a television flipping through channels really, really fast. But it's not like a scary channel, you know? Just... loud. And it just won't turn off.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah... yeah, I have. Um, it's actually been really bad lately. Like, I'll wake up—when I do manage to sleep, or when I wake up at 4 AM like I was saying—and I just have this... this incredibly heavy feeling right in the center of my chest. It's almost like a physical weight, you know? And it's just this deep, deep emptiness. 

Like, I live in this little condo, right? And I worked *so* hard to get it. I saved up for years from my bookkeeping job, I scrimped and saved, I didn't go out with friends so I could put away a down payment, and I finally got this place. I picked out the paint colors, I bought this really nice rug for the living room... I should be so happy there. It's my own space. But lately, I'll just be sitting on my couch, looking around at this place I practically killed myself to get, and I just feel... nothing. Or worse than nothing. I just sit there and I want to cry. 

And I don't even know *why* I want to cry. It's not like anything terrible happened that day. I just feel so incredibly down and drained, like all the color has just been washed out of everything. I'll just sit there staring at the wall, and the tears will just start welling up, and I just feel so sad and heavy and... just completely empty inside, even when I'm surrounded by all the things I worked so hard for. It's really awful. It's like I can't even enjoy my own life right now.
Do you find that your sleep gets better or worse when you're feeling less sad?

Well, that's the weird thing. When I'm not feeling so heavy and down, my sleep is... well, it's still messed up, but in a totally different way. Like, a few weeks ago, before this really bad slump hit, I wasn't sad at all. Actually, I felt pretty great. But my sleep was still completely off. 

The difference was, I wasn't lying there staring at the ceiling feeling drained, or waking up at 4 AM feeling like a zombie. I was just... not sleeping much at all, and I didn't even care. There were several nights in a row where I think I only slept maybe three or four hours total. I'd go to bed at like 2 AM because I was busy reorganizing my entire kitchen—like, taking everything out of the cabinets, wiping down the shelves, putting down new contact paper, alphabetizing my spices, the whole nine yards. And then my alarm would go off at 6 AM for work, and I'd just pop right out of bed. 

Normally, if I get three hours of sleep, I'm dragging. I need, like, a venti dark roast from Starbucks just to function. But during that time? I felt completely charged. I felt like I had electricity humming under my skin. I didn't even need coffee. I'd just bounce into the office, ready to tackle the spreadsheets, talking a mile a minute to the receptionist. So yeah, when I'm not feeling sad, my sleep doesn't really get *better*, it just changes from this awful, heavy insomnia to this weird state where I barely sleep at all but feel like I have all the energy in the world. It's like my body forgets it actually needs rest.
Do you always feel like you have a lot of energy when you're not feeling sad?

Well, it's not always... I mean, mostly, yeah, when I'm not in that awful, heavy place, I do tend to have a lot of energy. But sometimes it's more than just energy, it's like this intense drive to *do* things. 

Like, during that same time a few weeks ago, when I was only sleeping those three or four hours? I wasn't just reorganizing the kitchen. I was doing everything. I would get home from work—and keep in mind, I'd been doing bookkeeping for eight hours straight, staring at numbers, which usually leaves me completely fried—but I'd walk in the door and it was like a switch flipped. I'd start deep cleaning the bathroom, scrubbing the grout with a toothbrush. And then while the floor was drying, I'd sit at my laptop and start making these massive, incredibly detailed lists for renovating the condo. Like, pulling up Home Depot tabs, comparing the prices of brushed nickel versus matte black hardware for the cabinets, mapping out a whole budget on a spreadsheet. 

And then, I don't even know how, but that led me down this rabbit hole of checking mortgage interest rates, just in case I wanted to refinance, even though I just bought the place. I was reading all these financial blogs and calculating amortization schedules at like 11:30 at night. And *then*, because I was thinking about money, I decided I needed a side hustle. So I started outlining a business plan for doing freelance bookkeeping for small businesses in the area. I was looking up domain names, drafting cold emails to send to local coffee shops and boutiques... I mean, I was just going and going and going. It was like I had a motor inside me that I couldn't shut off. I just felt this absolute need to be productive, to fix things, to plan things, to start new projects. So yeah, I guess when I'm not sad, I don't just have energy... I have this crazy burst of activity where I feel like I can take on the entire world, all at once, usually after I've already worked a full day.
Do these periods of having a lot of energy and wanting to take on a lot of projects happen in distinct episodes, or is it more of a constant state when you're not feeling sad?

It's definitely in distinct episodes. It's not like a constant baseline thing. Like, when I'm just feeling normal—which honestly feels like a luxury these days—I'm just... normal. I go to work, I come home, I watch some TV, I go to bed. But these periods, like the one earlier in the month, they're like a switch gets flipped, you know? It's like a wave that just washes over me. 

Earlier in the month, it was exactly like that. I just woke up one day and felt almost... lit up. Like I was glowing from the inside out, and I felt completely unstoppable. Like every idea I had was brilliant and I had to execute it right that second. The kitchen, the business plan, the refinancing... it all felt so urgent and exciting. 

But the thing is, it wasn't just all positive, productive energy. It's like... because I felt so fast and so capable, everyone else felt like they were moving in slow motion, and it would just drive me crazy. I'd be in this unstoppable zone, and then my mom would call to ask me something totally mundane, like what time she should bring her car to the mechanic, and I would just snap at her. Like, really bite her head off. I'd be like, "Mom, I don't know, just look at the hours online, I'm busy!" And normally, I'd never talk to her like that. We have a good relationship. 

Or at work—I was doing my bookkeeping, flying through the spreadsheets, and my supervisor came over to ask a really simple question about one of the accounts. Something she asks me all the time, totally standard procedure. And I just felt this flash of pure annoyance, like, hot prickly irritation all over my neck. I had to bite my tongue so hard not to yell at her for interrupting my flow. I ended up giving her this really clipped, short answer, and she kind of looked at me weird and walked away. It's like, when I'm in one of those episodes, I'm so revved up that any little roadblock or question that wouldn't normally bother me at all just feels like this massive, infuriating obstacle. So yeah, it's definitely an episode, and it's not just energy... it's like this intense, impatient, irritable drive that just takes over for a while until I crash back down into that awful heavy feeling.
What happens to your mood and energy level after one of these episodes of feeling unstoppable and irritable ends?

Well, it's like... you know how a balloon looks when you let all the air out of it at once? It just kind of flops to the floor, completely deflated. That's exactly what happens to me. The motor just... dies. 

One day I'm alphabetizing the spices and drafting business plans, and then literally the next morning, or maybe a couple days later, I just wake up and it's gone. The energy is completely wiped out. And it's not just that I'm tired from not sleeping during that whole hyper phase, though I guess that's probably part of the physical side of it, but it's this mood shift that is just so drastic and overwhelming. 

Lately, when that crash happens, I wake up with this incredibly heavy, empty feeling. It's like someone poured lead into my veins overnight. I can't even explain how heavy my limbs feel. And the sadness is just... it's everywhere. I'll just be sitting there in my living room, looking around at my condo... and you have to understand, I worked *so* hard to buy this place. I started working right out of high school, doing data entry, working my way up to the bookkeeping position I have now, just saving every single penny I could so I wouldn't have to rent forever. I should be so proud of it, right? I mean, I *am* proud of it, normally. 

But when I'm in this awful slump, I'll just be sitting on the couch I saved up for, in this beautiful condo that I worked so hard for, and it just makes me want to cry. I'll just look at the walls and feel absolutely nothing but this crushing sadness. It doesn't make any rational sense. Why would I want to cry looking at my own biggest achievement? But I do. The tears just sit there behind my eyes all day. I can barely drag myself into the kitchen that I was just scrubbing with a toothbrush a week prior. It's just this dark, heavy cloud that settles over everything, and the emptiness is almost worse than the sadness, if that makes sense? Because when I was up, everything mattered *so* much, and then suddenly, absolutely nothing matters at all. I'll just sit there, staring at the brushed nickel cabinet hardware I spent three hours picking out online, and just... cry. It's just so exhausting to go from feeling like I own the world to feeling like I can't even exist in my own living room.
Do you always feel sad or empty after one of these episodes of high energy and irritability ends?

Well, lately, yeah. I mean, it feels like it's always that way right now. This... this really obvious cycling between that crazy, charged-up stretch and then this awful, heavy crash... it's been going on for about a month now. Basically ever since the mortgage actually became real. 

And what I mean by that is, you know, you sign the papers and it's all kind of a blur of legal jargon and excitement, but then about a month ago, I got the actual first official statement in the mail from the lender. I had just gotten home from work, and I was standing in the kitchen, and I opened the envelope, and seeing my name next to this massive amount of debt, the thirty-year commitment... it just made it all so real. It hit me like a ton of bricks. 

And literally ever since that day, about a month ago, it's just been this constant back and forth. I'll have a few days where I'm completely wired, scrubbing the floors, doing the freelance business plans, feeling like I can pay off the whole loan in five years if I just hustle hard enough... and then the motor just dies, and I crash right back into that empty, crying-on-the-couch phase where I can't even look at the walls without tearing up. It's just been a solid month of this really obvious bouncing back and forth, up and down, and it's just... I don't even know which version of me is going to wake up in the morning anymore. I mean, I guess I've always had days where I'm more tired than others, but this specific pattern? Going from being totally unstoppable to just completely hollowed out? That's been the last month, exactly since that piece of mail showed up and the house became this real, permanent thing. It’s exhausting, honestly, just going from one extreme to the other like this.
Do you ever go back to feeling normal after one of these high-energy episodes, or does it always end in that heavy, sad feeling?

Normal... gosh, I don't even know if I remember what normal actually feels like at this point. Because, well, if I'm being completely honest with myself—and I've been thinking about this a lot lately, just trying to retrace my steps and figure out where things went off the rails—this... this depressed, guilty fog hasn't just been happening for the last month. 

It’s actually been hanging around for about five months now. Five whole months of just... wading through wet cement. Back then, I was right in the middle of the really intense part of house hunting, and I just started feeling this awful, heavy weight settling over me. And the guilt... oh my gosh, the guilt was just suffocating. I'd be walking through these open houses with my realtor, looking at places I’d saved up for years to be able to afford, and I just felt like a total fraud. I should have been thrilled, you know? But instead, I was just dragging myself from room to room, feeling incredibly guilty that I wasn't excited, guilty that I was wasting everyone's time, guilty that I just wanted to go back to my rental and sleep for a week. I'd go into work at the bookkeeping firm and just stare at my screen, feeling so down and so useless, wondering why I couldn't just snap out of it and be happy like a normal twenty-six-year-old buying her first place.

So, no, I haven't really been going back to a "normal" baseline after these recent high-energy days. It's more like... that depressed, guilty fog was already my normal for five months. It was just this long, drawn-out slump. But it definitely got *much* worse after I actually bought the condo and everything became finalized a month ago. That's when the really dramatic crashes started happening. It’s like I was already stuck in this muddy, guilty hole for months, and then the reality of the mortgage hit, and now I’m having these days where I shoot out of the hole like a rocket, only to crash back down twice as deep as I was before. But yeah, the fog itself... that’s been sitting on my chest for a good five months. I just haven't felt like myself in such a long time.
Do you ever have one of these high-energy episodes without then feeling sad or empty afterwards?

I mean, I really wish I did. I honestly wish I could just have a day where I get all that stuff done, you know, the intense cleaning and the freelance business plans, and then just wake up the next day feeling like a regular person who just had a really productive weekend. But no, it never works out like that. Not once. It’s always, *always* followed by that awful drop. 

I can't think of a single time where the energy just... gently faded away and left me feeling okay. It's like... if you're driving a car a hundred miles an hour, you don't just get to coast to a nice, easy stop, you know? You hit a brick wall. That's exactly what it feels like. I don't get to just slowly wind down and feel fine. The energy just snaps, and that heavy sadness is instantly there waiting for me. 

I’ll go from feeling like I can conquer the world, maybe I'm organizing all my client files for the bookkeeping firm, getting way ahead of schedule, feeling absolutely fantastic and capable, and then... boom. The very next morning, or whenever the motor finally gives out, I can't even look at those same files without feeling like crying. So, no, I don't think I've ever had one of those energized times where I didn't end up completely miserable and empty right after. It's like a package deal, unfortunately. You don't get the high without paying for it with the low, and lately, the price is just... it's just so heavy. I keep waiting for a time when I just level out and feel okay after being so productive, but the sadness is just always right there, waiting for the energy to run out.
Is it always the case that after one of these high-energy episodes, you end up feeling sad or empty?

Yeah, like I was just saying, it really is. It never fails. I know I'm probably talking in circles a bit here, but it's just... it's so absolute, you know? There's no escaping it. 

Lately, especially, it’s been so intense. I'll just wake up with this heavy, empty feeling that I can't even really describe properly. It's like... I'll open my eyes in the morning, and before my feet even touch the floor, this massive weight is just already sitting on my chest. And it's so incredibly frustrating and confusing because I'll be sitting there in my own condo—this place that I worked *so* hard for, doing all those extra hours at the bookkeeping firm, saving every single penny for years—and instead of feeling proud or settled, just being there makes me want to cry. 

I'll literally just sit on the sofa that I saved up for, looking around at the walls I painted, and I just feel completely hollowed out. The tears just start falling, and I can't stop them. It makes no sense, right? I should be so happy with what I've accomplished, but after those energetic days burn off, all that's left is this... this awful, heavy emptiness where I'm just crying in the middle of my own living room. It's like the condo itself, which should be my biggest achievement, just turns into this big, sad box that I'm trapped in. So, yeah, it always, always ends up with me feeling that way. I just can't seem to get a break from that drop.
Is there ever a time when you have one of these high-energy episodes and it doesn't end with you feeling sad or empty?

I... I feel like we're going over the exact same thing again, but... I mean, I really don't mind explaining it again if it helps figure out what's wrong with me, because I am just so tired of living like this. But honestly, no. Never. There is never, ever a time when I get that burst of energy and it doesn't end in a total crash. 

Like I was saying before, about the condo and the crying... it's just a guarantee. It's like clockwork. I'll have that day where I'm buzzing, where I'm doing all the client files and feeling like I can take on the whole world, and then... it's gone. And I'm not just back to normal, I'm plunged right back into that awful, suffocating sadness. I wish I could tell you that sometimes I just level out, maybe just feel a little tired like a normal person who did too much over the weekend, but it never happens. It's always the energy, and then the emptiness. Every single time. I just... I don't know how else to explain it, it's just always that same cycle.
Is it possible for you to have one of these high-energy episodes without feeling sad or empty afterwards?

I... wait, I feel like maybe I'm not explaining myself right, or maybe you're testing my memory? Because you keep asking me if it's possible, and I keep saying no, it's really, absolutely not possible. I'm sorry, I don't mean to get frustrated with you, I know you're just doing your job, but I feel like a broken record here. 

No, it is never possible to just have the energy and be fine. It always, without fail, goes straight into that horrible drop. Like I was just trying to describe to you a second ago... lately I wake up with this incredibly heavy, empty feeling that just completely crushes me. It's right there the second I open my eyes. And it makes absolutely no logical sense, which is the most agonizing part of the whole thing. I'll be sitting right there in my own condo—the exact place I worked so unbelievably hard for, taking on all those extra auditing files and pinching pennies for years just to get the down payment—and instead of feeling secure or proud of myself, just sitting in that space makes me want to cry. I'll literally just sit there feeling completely hollowed out, crying my eyes out over absolutely nothing. 

So if you're asking if I can ever just have the productive, energetic days and somehow magically skip the part where I'm sobbing in my living room feeling completely empty... no. It is not possible. It happens every single time. Did I... did I answer it right this time? Because I honestly don't know how else to explain that I never, ever get to skip the sadness.
Is there ever a time when one of these episodes of high energy ends without being followed by a period of feeling sad or empty?

I... I'm sorry, I am genuinely so confused right now. Are you... is this some kind of specific psychological test where you have to ask the exact same thing four times to see if I change my answer? Because I feel like I'm losing my mind a little bit here. I really, truly don't know how to say it any differently. 

No. Never. There is never a time. It always, always ends with me feeling sad and empty. 

Like I've been trying to explain, lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling that just completely swallows me whole. It's just... it's so heavy I can barely breathe sometimes. And I'll be sitting right there in my own condo, which, you know, I worked so incredibly hard for—doing all those extra hours at the bookkeeping firm, staring at ledgers and spreadsheets until my eyes burned, saving every single paycheck just to finally get my own place—and even just sitting in that space makes me want to cry. It's supposed to be my safe haven, my biggest accomplishment, but I just sit there sobbing and feeling entirely hollowed out. 

So, no, the high energy never just fades away into a normal, regular day. I never get to just be okay afterwards. It always drags me right back down into that awful emptiness. I really, really hope you're writing that down this time, because I honestly don't think I have the words to explain it a fifth time.
Is it always the case that after one of these high-energy episodes, you end up feeling sad or empty?

I... okay. Okay, yes. Yes, it is always the case. I'm sorry, I just... I'm really trying not to get upset, but I feel like I'm trapped in some kind of loop here, and it's making me feel even more crazy than I already do. I don't know if I'm just not being clear enough, or if there's a specific word you're waiting for me to say, but... yes. Always. 100 percent of the time. 

It's like I was just saying... I'll have that burst of energy where I'm getting all my bookkeeping done, and then it's just gone. And lately, it's been so bad. I'll wake up with this heavy, empty feeling that's just... it's suffocating. It's like a physical weight on my chest before I even get out of bed. And I'll just sit there in my condo—the condo I literally gave up years of my life for, working overtime, auditing files until I couldn't see straight, skipping vacations just to save the money—and instead of feeling happy or proud, I just sit there and cry. It makes me want to cry just being in it, because I feel so completely hollow. 

So, yes. The answer is yes. It always ends with me feeling sad and empty. It never just goes away. It always ends in a crash. Always. Please tell me you understand what I'm saying this time.
Do you think your high-energy episodes might be related to your mood, or are they separate things?

I... I mean, I don't really know how to answer that. Are they related to my mood? I guess I don't really understand what you mean by "separate things." Like, is the energy my mood? Or is the sadness my mood? Because when I have that energy, when I'm just flying through my bookkeeping files and getting a month's worth of reconciliation done in three days, I feel... well, I feel energetic. I don't know if I'd call it a "mood" exactly, it's just this intense drive, like my brain is moving a million miles an hour and I have to keep up with it. 

But then, obviously, like I've been saying over and over, the sadness comes right after. And that's definitely a mood, right? That heavy, crushing emptiness where I'm just sitting on my sofa staring at the wall, crying in this condo I spent five years saving for. So... are they related? I mean, they happen back-to-back, so they must be connected somehow, but I don't know if the energy itself is a mood or if it's just... a thing that happens to my body and my brain before my mood completely tanks. I'm sorry, I'm probably overthinking this, but I just don't really know how to separate them or what exactly counts as a mood in this situation.
Do you think the energy and the sadness are two separate things that happen to you, or are they connected as part of the same emotional experience?

I mean... I don't know. I really don't know how to answer that, because I'm not a doctor, you know? I'm just a bookkeeper. I look at numbers all day, I don't look at... at brain chemicals or psychology or whatever makes this happen. 

Are they connected? Like I said, they happen one right after the other, so I guess they have to be connected, right? It's like... it's like a pendulum swinging. I swing all the way up into this crazy, intense energy where I'm just working and working and working, and my brain won't shut off, and I'm organizing every single receipt from the last three years, and then... then it swings all the way back down into that horrible, suffocating emptiness. 

But are they the *same* emotional experience? I don't know. They feel so incredibly different. The energy feels like... like electricity in my veins. And the sadness just feels like lead. Like I'm drowning in it. When I'm sitting there crying in my condo—which, again, I worked so hard for, I sacrificed so much for—it doesn't feel like the energy at all. It feels like the energy never even existed. It feels like I've just always been empty and I always will be. 

So I guess I just don't know. I don't know if they're two sides of the same coin or if my brain is just broken in two completely different ways. I just know that it happens, and it keeps happening, and I can't stop it, and I'm so exhausted by it. I just want to know if there's a way to make it stop, instead of just trying to figure out how to categorize it.
Do you think the high-energy episodes and the sadness that follows are part of the same mood cycle, or are they unrelated?

I... I feel like we are just going in circles here. Are you asking me the exact same question again? Because I really, truly don't know what else to tell you. I don't know what a "mood cycle" is supposed to mean. 

In my job, you know, in bookkeeping, I know what a billing cycle is. I know what an accounting cycle is. You open the books, you record the transactions, you reconcile the ledger, you close the books at the end of the month. That's a cycle. It makes sense. It has a clear beginning and an end and there are rules. But my brain? There are no rules. I don't know if this is a cycle. I just know that one week I am tearing through my apartment, color-coding my client folders and feeling like I could run a marathon while doing three months of back-taxes, and the next week I am a completely useless lump on my couch, crying my eyes out and wondering why I even bother paying the mortgage on this place. 

I don't know if that's a cycle or if it's just... my life falling apart in two completely different directions. Like I've been saying, they happen back-to-back. The energy, and then the crash. Every single time. So they aren't unrelated, obviously, because the crash always comes right after the energy. But if you're asking me to clinically define if they are "part of the same mood cycle"... I just don't have the answer for you. I'm not trying to be difficult, I promise, I just... I don't know what specific words you want me to use! I feel like I'm failing a test here. I just want to know how to fix it, I don't care what kind of cycle it is.
Do you believe the high-energy episodes and the sadness that follows are connected as part of the same emotional experience?

I... I really don't understand what is happening right now. Are we... is there a hidden camera in here or something? Because you are asking me the exact same thing again. Like, literally the exact same question you just asked me, just with slightly different words. 

I don't know what you want me to say about them being the "same emotional experience." I really, honestly don't. I've told you how the energy feels—like my brain is just buzzing and I'm getting all these ledgers balanced and everything is moving so incredibly fast—and I've told you how the sadness feels, like I'm just glued to the couch in my condo, crying for absolutely no reason and feeling totally worthless. So if you're asking me if they are the *same* experience, no, they feel completely, totally different! One is fast and productive, and the other is just... devastating. 

But if you're asking if they are connected... I mean, I just said they happen back-to-back. Every single time. The crash always follows the energy. Always. I'll have that crazy productive week where I'm unstoppable, and then boom, I'm at the bottom of a well. So yes, they are connected in time, obviously, but I don't know if they are connected in my... in my emotions? Or my brain chemistry? 

I just... I feel like you're looking for a very specific word from me, like a password or a secret code or something, and I don't know it. I only went to high school, okay? I learned how to do bookkeeping on the job, I worked my way up, I don't have a degree in psychology. I don't know the terminology. I just know that my life feels completely out of control right now, and sitting here debating the exact phrasing of whether it's one emotional experience or two separate emotional experiences isn't helping me figure out how to wake up tomorrow and actually function at my job. Can we please, please just talk about how to make the crashing stop? Because I really can't take answering this question a fifth time.
Do you consider your high-energy episodes to be a separate issue from your overall mood?

I... I actually can't believe this. Are you reading off a script? Is there some kind of mandatory checklist you have to get through where you just ask me the exact same thing five different ways? "Separate issue from my overall mood?" What does "overall mood" even mean? 

My mood is my mood! When I'm up and doing the books and flying through spreadsheets and I feel like I can take on the entire world, that's my mood right then. When I'm crying on the couch in my condo that I worked my butt off to buy, feeling like I can't even breathe, that's my mood right then. I don't have some baseline, normal "overall" mood that just sits there in the background while these other things happen to me. It's all just me. It's my life. 

So I don't know if it's a separate issue. I really, truly don't. Like, if a client comes to me and they have their payroll messed up, and they also have their quarterly taxes messed up, I don't sit there and ask them if it's a separate issue from their overall business model, I just fix the numbers!
